text:
maria: Quick flag — noticed a regression in decode tail latency on nightly after the kernel-selector change. Small-batch (<=3 requests, seq<=16) coldstarts spike ~20-30% since yesterday. trace: https://perf.redwood/trace/2098765432

sam: Ugh. Is this prefill or decode path?

maria: Decode path only. Prefill numbers look stable. I dumped a few traces, looks like we switched to the ‘flash_paged_v2’ kernel in decode for small batches and the KV cache page probing seems to be interfering.

alex: Can you paste the short profile? small snippets are fine.

maria: Sure — short output from Nsight sampling for a failing request: 
```
kernel=flash_paged_v2
batch_size=2
seq_len=12
kernel_launch_ms=0.75
kernel_exec_ms=1.9   # compare baseline fused_v1 exec 1.2ms
mem_copy_ms=0.4
kv_probe_ms=0.8
GPU_util=62%
```

jin: kv_probe_ms at 0.8 is alarming. Are we seeing extra page faults/cold reads? Maybe paged attention path does extra indexing per head for small batches.

sam: I briefly reran microbench on my local rig: when I force decode->fused_flash variant, latency returns to baseline. So selector prefers paged variant for memory reasons but loses perf on small-batch decode.

maria: Exactly. The selector heuristic uses estimated memory footprint and picks paged to reduce peak memory. For small-batch decode that's over-conservative and causes extra probing cost.

alex: Two actionable ideas: 1) add a small-batch override in selector to prefer fused flash for decode when batch<=3 OR seq<=32; 2) add a kv-probe fastpath for hot pages to avoid extra indexing overhead.

maria: I ran a quick A/B on canary: toggle selector to prefer fused_flash for decode when batch<=3 and saw 18% tail latency drop for the test workload. Throughput unchanged.

ops-ci-bot: ci/test-performance #3421 finished — compare: decode_smallbatch_p95: baseline 54ms -> canary 44ms (18% down).

jin: Nice. Need to check memory regression. Did peak mem grow?

maria: Peak mem up ~3% for that config on the canary, within our headroom for dedicated nodes. On lowest-tier boxes it would matter.

sam: Maybe make it a per-deployment policy: dedicated nodes use fused by default for small decode, hosted keeps paged for memory-constrained tiers. Add a flag in model config like "small_decode_prefer_fused": true/auto.

alex: Also add a metric: "kv_probe_count" and "kv_probe_ms" per request. Right now we only log total KV cache hits/misses. We need finer-grained probes to correlate.

maria: I added a quick PR with selector override + unit tests; pushing for canary rollout. PR: https://git.redwood/pr/1125 (notes in description).

sam: Can we add a microbench in eng-runtime nightly that sweeps batch size 1..8 and seq 8..64 for both kernels and outputs p95 and mem? We should catch this in CI before it lands.

bench-bot: scheduled perf-sweep job perf/attn-kernel-sweep-209876 at 03:00 UTC. Results will be posted to the perf dashboard.

jin: Also, let's capture a short reproducer with synthetic KV fragmentation (simulate many tiny key inserts) — sounds like fragmentation + paged path is the combo that regresses. Maria can you attach the reproducer in the PR?

maria: On it. I'll add reproducer script and a runbook: how to toggle selector flags, how to interpret kv_probe_ms. I'll also add a canary gating rule to prevent changing default on hosted until perf-sweep passes.

alex: One more thought: we should evaluate a hybrid kernel that uses fused flash but falls back to paged attention only when projected memory > X% — cheaper than full paged path. Might reduce probe overhead. I'll sketch an RFC.

maria: Thanks — happy path for now is selector override + metrics + perf sweep. If sweep looks good we can roll change for dedicated; hosted will stay conservative.

sam: lgtm. keep us posted, @maria. :thumbsup:

maria: Will do. I'll post canary links once the PR merges and perf jobs finish.
